iDynamics

A configurable emulation framework for evaluating microservice scheduling policies under controllable cloud–edge dynamics.

IEEE TSC · 2026·Early Access
Read paperExplore code
On this pageThe problemMy contributionDesign decisionsEvaluationLimitationsPaper & resources

The problem

A scheduling policy can look effective under one workload and struggle when traffic, network conditions, or application behavior changes. Comparing policies requires a way to control those changes and repeat the experiment.

My contribution

I developed a configurable framework that connects workload generation, evolving service call graphs, network emulation, and policy evaluation. The implementation uses aggregate Prometheus queries and sparse graph construction, with distributed network verification and per-run evidence records.

Design decisions

Make dynamics configurable

Represent workload and network changes as experimental inputs so that the same scenario can be replayed across scheduling policies.

Connect application and infrastructure views

Use service-level telemetry and call-graph information together with node-level network conditions to describe the environment a scheduler actually sees.

Evaluate the emulation itself

Measure how closely configured delay and bandwidth match observed behavior, alongside the effect of scheduling decisions.

Evaluation & outcomes

The framework was evaluated on a research testbed with one control-plane node and 45 workers. Delay-injection validation across 72 directed pairs in a nine-worker subset reported a mean absolute error of 0.274 ms. Mean relative bandwidth-shaping error was 4.28% in the reported validation.

45worker nodes in the evaluation testbed
0.274 msmean absolute delay error

What the results depend on

Emulation offers controlled conditions for comparing policies. Its results still depend on the selected applications, hardware, workloads, and configured dynamics; evaluation in another deployment requires fresh measurements.
